top_story: Israel’s campaign in Gaza continues to exact a severe civilian toll, with a damaged building sheltering about 100 displaced families collapsing in Gaza City on 16 September and killing at least 21 people, including 11 children, as rescue crews worked without heavy machinery and many remained trapped. The scale of displacement inside the building and the weak emergency capacity underscore how repeated strikes are compounding humanitarian fragility long after the initial blast. A day later, Washington approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35s to Saudi Arabia, advancing a major military upgrade for Riyadh as regional tensions remain tied to the Iran war and reinforcing a security order centered on deterrence and arms transfers. The juxtaposition is stark: US regional policy is deepening partner military capacity even as civilian protection and recovery in active war zones continue to erode.
